output.summary: NOV reported revenues of $1.25 billion and a net loss of $115 million for the first quarter of 2021 on a U.S. GAAP basis, marking a 6% sequential decline in consolidated revenue compared to the previous quarter. This drop was attributed to customer austerity, operational disruptions caused by severe winter weather in Texas and Oklahoma, and ongoing challenges from the pandemic affecting supply chains for critical materials like fiberglass and resin. Despite these headwinds, NOV noted early signs of recovery in the oilfield, particularly in its Wellbore Technologies segment, which saw sequential growth driven by improved pricing, cost reductions, and increasing rig activity in North America. The Completion & Production Solutions (CAPS) segment experienced a 20% sequential revenue decline due to depleted backlogs and supply chain issues, though it posted a book-to-bill ratio above 100%, indicating improving demand. The Rig Technologies segment faced weak capital equipment orders and a book-to-bill of 59%, yet the company expressed optimism about future rig deliveries from its new Saudi Arabia manufacturing plant. Looking ahead, NOV anticipates stronger results for the remainder of the year as oilfield activity rebounds, pricing normalizes, and cost-saving initiatives continue to yield benefits. Key uncertainties include the pace of recovery, global economic developments, and potential increases in oil supply from OPEC and Iran. The company also emphasized its focus on innovation and the energy transition, leveraging its expertise in next-generation technologies to support both traditional and emerging markets.
